Deterministic Overlapping Chunker for Long Clinical Transcripts

Source: R/workflow.R
chunk_clinical_texts.Rd

Splits long unstructured documents (such as therapy transcripts, qualitative interviews, or multi-page clinical histories) that exceed local LLM context windows into deterministic, overlapping chunks aligned on paragraph or sentence boundaries while preserving doc_id, chunk_index, character offsets, and unique chunk_id provenance for re-aggregation.

Usage

chunk_clinical_texts(
  data,
  text_col,
  id_col = NULL,
  max_chars = 3000L,
  overlap_chars = 250L,
  split_on = c("paragraph", "sentence", "character")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing documents to chunk.

text_col

Character scalar name of the text column in data.

id_col

Optional character scalar column name supplying unique document IDs. If NULL, synthesizes "1", "2", ..., "N".

max_chars

Positive integer maximum character length per chunk (minimum 50L, default 3000L).

overlap_chars

Non-negative integer character overlap carried from the end of each chunk into the start of the next chunk (must be strictly less than max_chars, default 250L).

split_on

Character scalar boundary preference: "paragraph" (default, prefers blank-line paragraph breaks before falling back to sentence/word breaks), "sentence", or "character".

Value

A tibble with columns doc_id, chunk_id, chunk_index, n_chunks, start_char, end_char, char_count, and chunk_text.

Examples

long_df <- tibble::tibble(
  doc_id = "T01",
  transcript = paste(
    rep("Patient described steady progress with sleep hygiene and mindfulness exercises.", 12),
    collapse = " "
  )
)
chunks <- chunk_clinical_texts(long_df, "transcript", id_col = "doc_id",
                               max_chars = 300L, overlap_chars = 60L)
chunks[, c("doc_id", "chunk_id", "chunk_index", "n_chunks", "char_count")]
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   doc_id chunk_id      chunk_index n_chunks char_count
#>   <chr>  <chr>               <int>    <int>      <int>
#> 1 T01    T01_chunk_001           1        4        240
#> 2 T01    T01_chunk_002           2        4        296
#> 3 T01    T01_chunk_003           3        4        296
#> 4 T01    T01_chunk_004           4        4        295
